[CW note] From the CryptoWeeklies video of 10 August 2026.

[2026-08-10_INJ]  
Video Title: Injective Risk Meter Flashes: What ML Models Project Next!  
Video ID: ivA_aGdA3mE  
Injective Protocol (INJ) | Class: CRYPTO  

    Current Structure:  
    • Current INJ price sits at a weekly average of $4.50, with a key short‑term support identified near $3.00 and a long‑term resistance around $6.50.  
    • The composite risk score places INJ in risk level 1, with a gravity risk index of 4.6–4.7, indicating a low‑risk, high‑euphoria environment for assets above market‑cap rank 20.  
    • Social sentiment analysis shows a markedly low social risk, reflecting a drop in altcoin interest; only 20% of the top 50 cryptos outperform Bitcoin in ROI, underscoring a Bitcoin‑season dominated market.  
    • The word‑cloud momentum for INJ highlights “euphoria” and “positive ROI” over the last 7 days, contrasting with a broader market negative ROI of -6.3% over 90 days.  

    Macro Quantitative Risk:  
    • The regression‑based fair value band places INJ at $6.50, one standard deviation below the model’s upper bound, signaling a current undervaluation of roughly 30% relative to fair value.  
    • TWAP baseline is implicitly anchored at the weekly average of $4.50; the TWAP risk level is low, with the price remaining above the green one‑standard‑deviation line but below the purple time‑average line.  
    • Historical lookback indicates that the last major bottom in March 2026 fell below the green line, followed by a rally to fair value and a rejection in early June, suggesting a cyclical pattern of bottom‑to‑fair‑value rebounds.  
    • Residual zones show that a 10‑week bearish run could push the bottom to approximately $2.10, while a bullish scenario could lift the price to a theoretical peak of $7.72 (a 70% upside from the current level).  

    Downside & Upside Targets:  
    • Machine‑learning forecasts project a non‑panic bear‑market bottom at about $2.10 (a 50% drop from the current $4.50), with a panic scenario capped at $2.70 and a three‑standard‑deviation scenario near $2.25.  
    • The regression‑based bottom‑identification module estimates a potential floor as low as $2.52, while the SMA model indicates a short‑term bubble peak around $3.40 before a decline to the $3.00 support.  
    • Upside targets include a cycle bull peak projected at $38 in 2029, implying an approximate 8× multiple of the current price, and a mid‑cycle rally that could reach $7.72 if the bullish zone is entered.  
    • Support floors are reinforced by the time‑average price (purple line) at a 60% discount, with historical evidence showing a premium evaporation to about 35% during prior rally phases.
